entries.question: Why is GPS confirmation of Special Relativity?
entries.heat: stackexchange/physics 2026-09-14, 15 points 5 comments, second highest physics score in today's pool
entries.why: GPS is the one relativity result a lay reader can already picture, and the popular framing (special relativity) is wrong in an interesting way: the gravitational term dominates and the net is a gain, not a loss.
entries.answer_angle: Separate the two clock terms. The 1905 speed term makes the satellite clock lose time; the gravitational blueshift of sitting higher in Earth's potential makes it gain more. The published offset is a design constant, so GPS is an operational check on the clock terms, not a clean single test of SR.
entries.use: qa-inject runner-up. Physics explainer paragraph for the relativity lore page; also a lead magnet for科普 audience.

entries.question: Can the relativistic effects on Mercury's orbit be reproduced in Newtonian mechanics by modifying Newton's gravity force law?
entries.heat: stackexchange/physics 2026-09-17 new thread, 9 points 3 comments, highest scoring question posted in the last 48h
entries.why: Freshest high-score question of the cycle. The honest answer is a real result: a velocity-dependent correction to the inverse-square law can be fitted to reproduce the observed perihelion advance, which is why the precession alone never proved general relativity.
entries.answer_angle: Fitting an extra term and predicting an unmeasured effect are different claims. A modified force law with velocity dependence can be tuned to the precession number; what separated GR was its other predictions (light bending, gravitational redshift, Shapiro delay) coming out of the same one-parameter theory.
entries.use: Long-tail SEO. Answers the 'was Einstein even needed' family of queries; pairs with the GPS条目 to build a relativity cluster.

entries.question: Magnetization v/s Polarization: Why are they weirdly dissimilar?
entries.heat: stackexchange/physics 2026-09-18 new thread, 2 points 1 comment, the newest E&M question in the pool
entries.why: Clean conceptual asymmetry with a crisp cause: isolated electric charge exists, magnetic poles do not. No fabricated data needed and the answer maps straight onto the field-shaping lore page.
entries.answer_angle: Polarization is sourced by separated charge; magnetization is sourced by circulating bound current. The D/H split exists so each field has a version that depends only on free sources. The asymmetry is a statement about sources, not about the fields.
entries.use: qa-inject primary. Fills the E&M slot on the field-control lore page, which has had no FAQ block for two cycles.

entries.question: Can thermodynamics macrostates hide relevant quantum information?
entries.heat: stackexchange/physics 2026-09-18 new thread, 1 point 0 comments, newest question of the day
entries.why: Direct line into coarse-graining and information loss, which is exactly the fiction layer's premise, and the honest physics answer (entropy is counting, not erasure of a fact) is genuinely clarifying.
entries.answer_angle: A macrostate is a coarse-grained description, so information is lost to the description, not from the system. Quantum correlations can survive coarse-graining as quantities that the macrostate does not track, which is why entanglement entropy and thermodynamic entropy are different counts.
entries.use: Lore-track long tail. Information and entropy queries feed the holography page; no injection this cycle.

entries.question: Is maximizing quantum-speed-limit saturation a known clock-selection criterion in relational quantum mechanics?
entries.heat: stackexchange/physics 2026-09-18 new thread, 0 points 0 comments, unanswered
entries.why: The asker is proposing a criterion and asking whether it exists in the literature, which is the honest-answer shape: say what the speed limit is, then say the clock-selection proposal is not established.
entries.answer_angle: The quantum speed limit bounds how fast a state can become distinguishable given an energy spread; that part is standard. Using its saturation to pick a preferred clock in a relational framework is not a settled criterion, so the answer separates the established bound from the speculative selection rule.
entries.use: Lore-track only. Good example of the two-layer rule; heat is zero so it must not be presented as popular.

entries.question: High-altitude blimp on Venus: shortsleeves weather?
entries.heat: stackexchange/space 2026-09-17 new thread, 1 point 0 comments, newest space question of the day
entries.why: The habitable-layer idea is a real mission concept and the asker's naive framing invites a precise correction about pressure, temperature and sulphuric acid at altitude rather than a yes or no.
entries.answer_angle: At roughly 50 km the pressure and temperature are close to Earth surface values, which is why the concept is studied. The chemistry is not benign: the cloud deck is sulphuric acid, and the wind regime means a platform drifts with the super-rotating atmosphere. Do not quote a specific temperature or pressure figure unless sourced.

entries.question: Did Earth's rotational slowing down contribute to its 23.5 degree axial tilt, or was it determined by early impacts?
entries.heat: stackexchange/space 2026-09-17 new thread, 0 points 0 comments, unanswered
entries.why: Removes a common misconception: tidal despinning changes spin rate, not the direction of the spin axis, so the tilt has to come from the formation and impact history.
entries.answer_angle: Angular momentum is directional, so slowing the spin changes magnitude, not the axis orientation. Tidal friction transfers spin angular momentum to the Moon's orbit; the tilt is set by the accreted and impact history. Precession moves the axis around a cone without changing the tilt angle.
entries.use: Lore-track. Rotation, torque and resonance cluster for the torsion page.

entries.question: Are there stable orbits of point masses around a massive cylindrical object?
entries.heat: stackexchange/space 2026-09-09, 8 points 1 comment, second highest space score in the pool
entries.why: Real geometry question with a real answer class: the exterior field of an infinite cylinder differs from a point mass, so orbital behaviour changes qualitatively and no circular orbit is stable in the naive sense.
entries.answer_angle: The potential of an extended body is not the point-mass potential, so 'orbit' has to be redefined. Bound motion can exist around a cylinder, but the stability properties and the absence of closed planar orbits are what make the answer non-trivial. Keep the derivation qualitative.
entries.use: Lore-track, geometry-heavy. Good for the arena page and for hard-SF readers who check the mechanics.

entries.question: Can I avoid having my planet become tidally locked to its star so quickly?
entries.heat: stackexchange/worldbuilding 2026-09-18 new thread, 2 points 1 comment, freshest worldbuilding question of the day
entries.why: The locking timescale is set by a small number of physical levers (tidal dissipation, orbital distance, star mass), so the answer gives the author adjustable knobs instead of a verdict.
entries.answer_angle: Locking time scales steeply with orbital distance and with the tidal dissipation factor, so a thicker crust, a larger orbit or a different dissipation efficiency all buy time. A resonance with another body can also pump eccentricity and delay the end state. No fabricated numbers.
entries.use: Lore-track and strong worldbuilding audience pull. Resonant spin-orbit states are the direct hook for the torsion page.

entries.question: Would it be plausible for a gas and ice belt to shield a planet from radiation?
entries.why: Separation of concerns question: a belt can absorb some flux but a diffuse belt has little column density, so shielding depends on where the planet is relative to the belt and the source.
entries.answer_angle: Attenuation depends on column density and material, so a thin diffuse belt is a poor shield while a dense inner torus could absorb a meaningful fraction of a directional flux. Geometry matters more than composition for an isotropic background. Avoid quoting attenuation figures without a source.
entries.use: Lore-track. Radiation and detection vocabulary feeds the sensing page.
